mcqs.question: What is the 'Prime Goal' of foreign policy?

options.b: Study the national cultural aspect of the nation
options.c: To protect, preserve and promote national interest

mcqs.explanation: The primary objective and fundamental goal of any nation's foreign policy is to safeguard its sovereignty, security, and well-being by protecting, preserving, and promoting its core national interests on the international stage[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is/are the major features of the foreign policy of Nepal?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal's foreign policy is anchored heavily on the principles of Non-alignment (NAM) and the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchasheel), making statements 1 and 4 the core features[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following does not come under the five principles of Panchasheel?
mcqs.explanation: The Five Principles of Panchasheel include mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty, mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference in internal affairs, equality and cooperation, and peaceful co-existence. 'Security' is not one of these specific principles[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the first country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
mcqs.explanation: The United Kingdom (UK) is the first country to establish formal diplomatic relations with Nepal, dating back to the peace treaty of 1923 and formal exchange of missions[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When did Nepal establish diplomatic relation with America?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal established formal diplomatic relations with the United States of America on April 25, 1947 AD[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the latest country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
mcqs.explanation: Among the options and recent records, the Republic of Kiribati represents the latest country with whom Nepal established formal diplomatic ties[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the First SAARC country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal established formal diplomatic relations with India on June 13, 1947, making it the first SAARC nation to do so[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who was the prime minister of Nepal at the time of diplomacy with Pakistan?
mcqs.explanation: B.P. Koirala served as the Prime Minister of Nepal when diplomatic relations were established with Pakistan[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When was Nepal maintained diplomatic relationship with Sri Lanka?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal established formal diplomatic relations with Sri Lanka (then Ceylon) in 1957 A.D[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the latest SAARC country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
mcqs.explanation: Bhutan is the latest SAARC country among the regional member states to establish formal diplomatic relations with Nepal on June 03, 1983[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not constructed with the aid of Japan?
mcqs.explanation: The Hetauda Diesel Plant was established with assistance other than Japanese aid, whereas infrastructure like the Kathmandu Bus Terminal (Gongabu), Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, and Udaypur Cement plant involve Japanese cooperation[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following was not constructed by the Russian government's assistance?

options.c: Pathalaiya - Dhalkebar Segment of Mahendra Highway

mcqs.explanation: Farping Hydropower Station is Nepal's first hydropower plant, built in 1911 under the premiership of Chandra Shumsher with British/local engineering, not by Russian assistance[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following was not constructed by the Chinese government's assistance?
mcqs.explanation: The LamoSaghu - Jiri road was constructed with Swiss assistance, while the Ring Road, Prithvi Highway, and Araniko Highway are well-known projects supported by Chinese aid[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When was the General Assembly of the United Nations approved the flag of the UN?
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations General Assembly officially approved the design of the UN flag on October 20, 1947[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The United Nations Charter was signed in which of the following cities?
mcqs.explanation: The UN Charter was signed on June 26, 1945, at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization in San Francisco[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which conference established the United Nations (UNO)?
mcqs.explanation: The San Francisco Conference (formally the United Nations Conference on International Organization) drafted and established the UN Charter in 1945[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When did UNO came into existence?
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations officially came into existence on October 24, 1945, after the Charter had been ratified by the permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of other signatories[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Currently, how many member nations are there in the United Nations organization?
mcqs.explanation: There are currently 193 member states in the United Nations organization[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the following 193rd member of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: South Sudan became the 193rd member state of the United Nations on July 14, 2011[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the purpose of the UN?

options.a: To develop friendly relationship among nations on the basis of equality
options.b: To be a centre for harmonizing the action of nations
options.c: To achieve national cooperation in resolving economic
options.d: To maintain international peace and security

mcqs.explanation: The UN's purpose is to achieve *international* cooperation (not national) in solving international economic, social, cultural, or humanitarian problems[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Branches of which tree appear on the UN flag?
mcqs.explanation: The UN flag features a map of the world embraced by olive tree branches, symbolizing world peace[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who coined the name of 'United Nations'?
mcqs.explanation: US President Franklin D. Roosevelt first coined and used the term 'United Nations' during the Second World War[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an official language of the United Nations?
mcqs.explanation: Portuguese is not an official language of the UN. The six official languages are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following set of language is not UN General Assembly official language?
mcqs.explanation: Japanese is not an official language of the UN General Assembly, making option (c) incorrect as a set[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many countries were there in the existence of period of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: There were 51 original member countries (founding members) when the UN came into existence in 1945[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following country was the last country to sign the Charter of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: Poland was not represented at the San Francisco Conference, but its signature was later added to the UN Charter, making it the 51st founding member (the last original signatory)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The Charter of UNO consists of
mcqs.explanation: The UN Charter is structured into 19 chapters containing a total of 111 articles[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many articles are there in United Nation's Charter?
mcqs.explanation: The UN Charter consists precisely of 111 articles distributed across 19 chapters[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The Headquarters of UNO, officially established in 1951 January 09, is located in
mcqs.explanation: The permanent headquarters of the United Nations is officially located in New York City, USA[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is/are an objective(s) of the UNO Charter?

options.b: To maintain international peace and security

mcqs.explanation: The objectives laid out in the UN Charter encompass maintaining peace and security, protecting human rights, and promoting social and economic development[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The UN Charter is concerned with
mcqs.explanation: The scope of the UN Charter binds and addresses all organs, member states across the General Assembly and Security Council, and the collective international community[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which country is the first to withdraw its membership of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: Indonesia became the first country to withdraw its UN membership in 1965 (though it resumed cooperation later)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of following given statement(s) is/are correct?

options.a: Currently, there 193 member nations in the United Nations organization
options.b: South Sudan is the 193rd member of UNO
options.c: The last country to sign the Charter of UNO was Poland

mcqs.explanation: All the listed statements accurately describe historical and current facts regarding UN membership[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which body of the United Nations Organizations is composed of all member states?
mcqs.explanation: The General Assembly is the main deliberative organ and is composed of all member states of the United Nations[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which organ of the United Nations Organizations is responsible for coordinating the work of its specialized agencies?
mcqs.explanation: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) coordinates economic, social, and related work of the 14 UN specialized agencies, functional commissions, and regional commissions[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who was the first woman president of United Nation General Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit of India was elected as the first woman President of the UN General Assembly in 1953 (8th session)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the first country whose membership of UNO was dissolved?
mcqs.explanation: Taiwan's representation and membership in the UN was replaced by the People's Republic of China in 1971 under Resolution 2758[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is/are a function(s) of the UN General Assembly?

options.a: Any matter affecting International peace & Security
options.b: It passes UN budget of the UN.
options.c: It elects the Non- permanent members of the Security Council

mcqs.explanation: The General Assembly discusses matters of international peace, approves the UN budget, and elects non-permanent members to the Security Council[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the main body of the United Nation organization?
mcqs.explanation: The General Assembly is considered the central deliberative and main representative body of the UN organization[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who is the person to deliver the longest speech in the General Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: Cuban leader Fidel Castro holds the record for delivering one of the longest speeches in the UN General Assembly history on September 26, 1960, lasting over 4 hours[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following organs of the United Nations Organization elects judges of the International court of Justice?

options.b: The Security Council and the General Assembly
options.c: The trusteeship council and the economic and social council

mcqs.explanation: Judges of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) are elected independently by both the UN General Assembly and the Security Council voting concurrently[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which General Assembly was conducted as the millennium General Assembly by UNO?
mcqs.explanation: The 55th session of the UN General Assembly in 2000 was designated as the Millennium Assembly, leading to the Millennium Declaration[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which countries are the Permanent of the Security Council of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: The five permanent members (P5) of the UN Security Council are China, Russia, the United States, the United Kingdom, and France[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many members of the United Nation's Security Council have veto power?
mcqs.explanation: All 5 permanent members of the Security Council possess veto power over substantive resolutions[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not permanent member of Security Council?
mcqs.explanation: Germany is not a permanent member of the UN Security Council; France, China, and the UK are among the P5[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: In which year was Nepal first elected on a Non-Permanent member of the united Nation Security Council?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal was first elected as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for the 1969–1970 term in the year 1969 AD[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Nepal had been the temporary member of UN Security Council for tenure
mcqs.explanation: Nepal has served as a non-permanent (temporary) member of the UN Security Council for 2 terms historically (1969-1970 and 1988-1989)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The total number of members in Security Council of UN?
mcqs.explanation: The UN Security Council consists of 15 members in total (5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many temporary members should be there in the provision of UNO Security Council?
mcqs.explanation: Under the UN Charter provisions, there are 10 non-permanent (temporary) members elected for two-year terms[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is/are true regarding UN Security Council?

options.a: The first country to use veto power is Russia
options.b: The country to use veto for most number of times is Russia
options.c: The country to use least veto power is France

mcqs.explanation: All statements are factually accurate: Russia (formerly USSR) was the first to use the veto, has used it the most times, while France has exercised it the least among the P5[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Human Rights Council in the United Nations is the subsidiary organ of
mcqs.explanation: The UN Human Rights Council (UNHRC) is a subsidiary body of the United Nations General Assembly[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Nepal had been the member of UN economic and Social Council for tenure.
mcqs.explanation: Nepal has been elected to membership of the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) for 3 terms[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many member counties are there in Economic and Social Council?
mcqs.explanation: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) is composed of 54 member states elected by the General Assembly[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When was the International Court of Justice was established?
mcqs.explanation: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) was established in 1946 as the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, replacing the Permanent Court of International Justice[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The headquarters of International Court of Justice is located in
mcqs.explanation: Unlike most other UN organs located in New York or Geneva, the ICJ has its headquarters at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many members are there in the International Court of Justice and what is their tenure?
mcqs.explanation: The ICJ is composed of 15 judges elected to 9-year terms of office by the General Assembly and Security Council[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following nation has withdraw its membership from international court of criminal (ICC) in recent time?
mcqs.explanation: The Philippines formally withdrew its membership from the International Criminal Court (ICC) following disputes regarding investigations into its domestic drug policies[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who are the members of the United Nations Trusteeship Council?

options.a: All members of the General Assembly
options.b: All members of the Security Council
options.c: Permanent members of the Security Council
options.d: Members of the Economic and Social Council

mcqs.explanation: The Trusteeship Council consists of the five permanent members of the Security Council (China, France, Russia, UK, US)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Trusteeship Council suspended its operation since
mcqs.explanation: The Trusteeship Council formally suspended its operations on November 1, 1994, after Palau, the last trust territory, attained independence[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Why did the Trusteeship Council suspend its operation?

options.a: Due to the used of USA veto
options.c: due to completion of its mandate
options.d: due to disputes between Member States

mcqs.explanation: It suspended operations because all trust territories had achieved self-government or independence, thereby completing its core mandate under the UN Charter[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who was the first Secretary General of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: Trygve Lie of Norway served as the first officially appointed Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1946 to 1952[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which country does the ninth secretary-general of UNO Mr. Antonio Guterres belong?
mcqs.explanation: António Guterres, the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations, is a former Prime Minister and citizen of Portugal[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Antonio Guterres becomes the Secretary General to visit Nepal.
mcqs.explanation: António Guterres was the 6th UN Secretary-General to make an official visit to Nepal (visiting in late 2023)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who was the first Secretary General of UNO to visit in Nepal?
mcqs.explanation: U Thant of Burma (Myanmar) was the first UN Secretary-General to visit Nepal, arriving in 1967[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who is the Secretary General of UNO died in plane Crash?
mcqs.explanation: Dag Hammarskjöld died in a mysterious plane crash in Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia) in 1961 while on a peace mission regarding the Congo crisis[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which Secretary-General of UN presented The Quiet Revolution Concept Paper?
mcqs.explanation: Kofi Annan presented reform proposals and concepts associated with organizational changes often referred to under administrative reform frameworks like 'The Quiet Revolution'[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which organ of the United Nations cannot be attended by the Secretary General of the United Nations?
mcqs.explanation: The International Court of Justice is an independent judicial tribunal; the Secretary-General is not a member and does not attend its judicial deliberations as an active participating organ official[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: For how many years is the Secretary General working period at a time?
mcqs.explanation: The UN Secretary-General is appointed for a term of 5 years by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which Secretary General of United Nations, presented the report called Blue print agenda?
mcqs.explanation: Boutros Boutros-Ghali presented comprehensive reports and agenda frameworks for peace and development, notably including structural blueprints during his tenure (such as An Agenda for Peace)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Secretary General of United Nations, whom was awarded with the Nobel Prize in Peace for the year 1961 A.D.?
mcqs.explanation: Dag Hammarskjöld was posthumously awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1961 for his humanitarian and diplomatic efforts[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following Specialized Agencies of United Nations awarded Noble peace prize for two times?

options.c: International Committees of the red cross

mcqs.explanation: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize twice (in 1954 and 1981)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following Organization awarded Noble peace prize for three times?

options.c: International committee of the Red Cross

mcqs.explanation: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize three times (1917, 1944, and 1963)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When did international labor organization (ILO) received the Nobel Peace Prize?
mcqs.explanation: The International Labour Organization (ILO) received the Nobel Peace Prize on its 50th anniversary in 1969 A.D[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When did International UNICEF received the Nobel Peace Prize?
mcqs.explanation: UNICEF was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965 for its worldwide efforts to protect and promote children's welfare[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: At which article of United Nations Charter, establishment of specialized agencies are mentioned?
mcqs.explanation: Article 57 of the UN Charter provides for the establishment and coordination of specialized agencies through ECOSOC[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: What is the first specialized agency of UNO?
mcqs.explanation: The International Labour Organization (ILO), originally created in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles, became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which UN Organization became the first to accept a donation in crypto currency?
mcqs.explanation: UNICEF established a cryptocurrency fund, making it the first UN agency to accept and hold contributions in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ether[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following UN agencies focuses on poverty reduction and the improvement of living standards worldwide?
mcqs.explanation: The World Bank group focuses heavily on providing financial and technical assistance for international development and poverty reduction[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not organ of United Nations?
mcqs.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is a specialized agency of the UN, not one of the six principal organs defined in the UN Charter[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a World Bank group of five institutions?
mcqs.explanation: The International Development Association (IDA) is one of the five constituent institutions forming the World Bank Group[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The headquarters of International Atomic Energy Agency is located in
mcqs.explanation: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: WTO came into existence in the year
mcqs.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO) officially came into existence on January 1, 1995, following the Marrakesh Agreement which replaced GATT[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a specialized agency of the United Nations Organization?
mcqs.explanation: The World Trade Organization (WTO) operates independently with its own treaty framework and is not technically classified as a UN specialized agency, unlike WHO, WMO, and WIPO[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not the organ of United Nation?
mcqs.explanation: The 'Peace Keeping Coordination Council' is a fictitious or non-existent principal organ; the six main organs are the General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ, and Secretariat[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not function of United Nations Development Program (UNDP)?
mcqs.explanation: Protecting refugees worldwide is the specific mandate of UNHCR, whereas UNDP focuses on poverty reduction, governance, crisis recovery, and environmental sustainability[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: From which institution the concept of good governance has developed?
mcqs.explanation: The World Bank popularized and formally articulated the concept of 'good governance' in its 1989 report on sub-Saharan Africa[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not the organ of United Nation?
mcqs.explanation: Similar to question 84, the Peace Keeping Coordination Council is not a principal organ of the UN[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Match the Group I with Group II and choose the correct answer.
mcqs.explanation: Matching the organizations with their host/associated countries or headquarters context: IMF is in USA (Washington, D.C.) -> a3; ILO is in Switzerland (Geneva) -> b4; FAO is in Italy (Rome) -> c2; ICAO is in Canada (Montreal) -> d1. This gives combination a3, b4, c2, d1[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Where is United Nations University located?
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations University (UNU) has its headquarters and central academic hub located in Tokyo, Japan[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following UN agencies has its headquarters at Paris
mcqs.explanation: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) is headquartered in Paris, France[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not an agency of UNO?

options.c: International Committee of the Red Cross

mcqs.explanation: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is an independent humanitarian institution, not a specialized or official agency of the United Nations[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The headquarters of Food and Agriculture Organization is in..........
mcqs.explanation: The headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is located in Rome, Italy[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The headquarters of World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is located in ............
mcqs.explanation: WIPO has its headquarters located in Geneva, Switzerland[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When ILO became a specialized agency of UN?
mcqs.explanation: Although founded in 1919, the ILO officially became the first specialized agency associated with the United Nations in 1946[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following UN agencies has received Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 A.D.?
mcqs.explanation: The World Food Programme (WFP) was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for its efforts in combating hunger and food insecurity in conflict areas[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following agencies assesses the 'LDC Graduation'?
mcqs.explanation: The Committee for Development Policy (CDP) under the UN framework (UNO) assesses and reviews Least Developed Country (LDC) graduations[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: In which Country, UNO has spent highest quantity of Budget?
mcqs.explanation: Historically, large peacekeeping or transitional administration operations such as the UNTAC mission in Cambodia accounted for substantial budget allocations during their respective eras[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The mission to which nation has been declared as the UN's most dangerous Peace keeping Mission?
mcqs.explanation: MINUSMA in Mali was widely categorized by UN reports as one of the most dangerous active peacekeeping missions due to asymmetric warfare and terrorist threats[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When was the Convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women issue
mcqs.explanation: CEDAW (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women) was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1979[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: As of August, 2024, there are member states as the parties on UN convention agang Corruption.
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) had reached 191 state parties by August 2024[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: In which year, UN celebrated international peace on;
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations observed 1986 as the International Year of Peace[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The United Nations General Assembly has declared 2026 as the......

options.b: International Year of Fruits and Vegetables
options.d: International Year of the Woman Farmer

mcqs.explanation: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer to highlight their vital contributions to food security and rural economies[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which period was declared to mark as 'World Decade of Indigenous Language' by United Nations
mcqs.explanation: The UN declared the period from 2022 to 2032 as the International Decade of Indigenous Languages[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Nepal was attained membership of UNO in
mcqs.explanation: Nepal officially became a member of the United Nations on December 14, 1955, as part of a historic package deal of admissions[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When was Nepal elected to the UN Security Council as a non-permanent membership for the first time?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal served its first non-permanent term on the UN Security Council during the years 1969-1970[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who is the first permanent representative of Nepal to participate in UN General Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: Rishikesh Shah served as Nepal's first permanent representative to the United Nations and represented Nepal in the General Assembly following admission[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who is the present permanent representative of Nepal in UN General Assembly?
mcqs.explanation: Ambassador Lok Bahadur Thapa serves as Nepal's permanent representative to the United Nations[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: The first Nepalese prime minister to address UN general Assembly is
mcqs.explanation: B.P. Koirala was the first Prime Minister of Nepal to address the United Nations General Assembly in person (during the 15th session in 1960)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When did Nepal participate in United Nations peace-keeping force as an observer for the first time
mcqs.explanation: Nepal first participated in UN peacekeeping operations in an observer capacity (UNOGIL in Lebanon) in 1958 AD[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: In which country did Nepal work as a peacekeeper for the first time under the United Nations?
mcqs.explanation: Lebanon marked Nepal's initial deployment area for observer and peacekeeping missions (such as UNOGIL/UNIFIL)[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: According to UN Peacekeeping Missions Report -2023, Nepal is the contributing country in UN Peace keeping Operations.
mcqs.explanation: Nepal consistently ranks among the top troop-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping operations globally, frequently appearing near or at the very top (1st) in official reports[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Of which organization among the following has Nepal become the member at first?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal joined the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) as its first major specialized agency membership prior to joining others[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When was Nepal became the member of World Trade Organization (WTO)?
mcqs.explanation: Nepal formally became the 147th member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) on April 23, 2004, being the first LDC to join through formal working party negotiations[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Nepal first attained the membership of Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in
mcqs.explanation: Nepal officially attained its membership in the FAO on November 21, 1951[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: When and under which treaty was SAARC officially established?
mcqs.explanation: SAARC was officially established with the adoption of its Charter at the first summit held in Dhaka, Bangladesh, in December 1985[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following given dignitaries is/are not the signatories on the Charter of SAARC?
mcqs.explanation: Ziaur Rahman initiated the concept of SAARC earlier, but he was assassinated in 1981; thus, the founding summit in 1985 was signed by then President Hussain Muhammad Ershad of Bangladesh, not Ziaur Rahman[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who was first raised the concept of regional, political and economical cooperation in South Asia?
mcqs.explanation: Bangladeshi President Ziaur Rahman formally proposed the creation of a regional trade and cooperation bloc in South Asia in the late 1970s[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an objective of the SAARC charter?

options.a: To promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia
options.c: To accelerate economic growth in South Asia
options.d: To contribute to mutual trust in South Asia

mcqs.explanation: Maintaining *international* peace globally is the UN's charter objective; SAARC's charter focuses on regional welfare, economic acceleration, cultural growth, and mutual trust within South Asia[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: For which of following, the SAARC movement was launched?
mcqs.explanation: SAARC was launched primarily to promote collective self-reliance and regional cooperation in economic, social, and cultural fields[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which of the following given is/are the principles of SAARC?
mcqs.explanation: SAARC cooperation is based on respect for sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, and mutual benefit[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many articles are there in Charter of SAARC?
mcqs.explanation: The Charter of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) consists of 10 articles[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: How many Apex bodies are there in SAARC?
mcqs.explanation: There are 6 recognized SAARC Apex bodies (such as SAARC CCI, SAARCLAW, etc.) that have formal institutional status[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which is the executive body of SAARC?
mcqs.explanation: The Standing Committee, comprising Foreign Secretaries of member states, acts as the core executive and monitoring body of SAARC[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: In which Article of the SAARC Charter, the principles of the SAARC is mentioned?
mcqs.explanation: Article II of the SAARC Charter outlines the general principles governing cooperation, sovereignty, and non-interference[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Which country is not the founder member of the SAARC?
mcqs.explanation: Afghanistan joined SAARC much later as the 8th member state during the 14th Summit in 2007; it is not a founding member[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who are the members of Council of Ministers of SAARC?

options.a: Ministers of foreign/external affairs of the members state
options.b: Ministers of prime ministers of the members state
options.c: Ministers of defence ministers of the members state
options.d: Ministers of home ministers of the members state

mcqs.explanation: The Council of Ministers of SAARC is composed of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs or External Affairs of each member state[cite: 8].

mcqs.question: Who is the Nepali artist to design the SARRC emblem?
